scope: All 12 previously deferred Luckfox/Sipeed/Brisbane/Trenz mini-computing entries; targeted follow-up of the 85-entry mini-computing audit, not a second whole-catalog audit.
policy: Preserve every published component ID, pin ID, electrical definition, native SVG and KiCad output. Source-reviewed coordinates activate only on new explicitly fitted breadboard-view instances. A source gap is distinct from an incompatible physical pattern. Nominal-post inference and stale CAD metadata are recorded explicitly; no global fit tolerance was changed.

entries.reason: Source identity mismatch, not a pitch exclusion: the catalog explicitly describes a distinct Luckfox USB-C/microSD board. Luckfox current Pico2 pinout and its linked Hardware/Schematic/Pico-2-schematic.pdf and Docs/datesheet/Pico-2-datasheet.pdf actually identify the official Raspberry Pi Pico 2 (micro-USB, no microSD). That PDF explicitly confirms 40 main 2.54 mm breadboard-compatible contacts, but it does not establish the different physical board currently represented by this published entry. Do not silently substitute a Raspberry Pi PCB or invent its auxiliary centers; the exact catalog hardware identity must first be corrected/reconciled.

The 3923 assembly and manufacturer 3921 dimension drawing corroborate the unchanged 40-hole, 20.32 mm mechanical family. This is a documented compatible-family nominal-header inference, not a claim that the stale 3920 title is exact revision-3923 production CAD.

entries.reason: Resolved against exact manufacturer 3072 TOP DXF. Its two complete HN1X10 header blocks have X=-14.49999894/+14.49999894 mm, separation 28.99999788 mm; Y=-14.13499586+i*2.54 mm, ten positions. Longitudinal pitch is compatible, but 29 mm row separation is not an integer multiple of 2.54 mm (nearest 27.94/30.48 mm). This is a genuine full-pattern mismatch; scaling the PCB or widening the fit tolerance would misrepresent the hardware. Use an adapter or jumpers.
